claim: The two components of structural uncertainty—across-trial ranking instability and within-trial candidate ambiguity—relate oppositely to reasoning accuracy: within-trial ambiguity correlates positively with correctness on reasoning tasks, while across-trial instability correlates negatively.
falsifier: On a new set of reasoning tasks, compute the correlation of each component with accuracy: within-trial ambiguity should show a positive correlation, across-trial instability a negative correlation, replicating the opposite-sign pattern.

exclusions: limited to the five LLMs and eight benchmarks studied; transfer beyond these systems and tasks is unestablished

title: Across-trial ranking instability–reasoning accuracy principle
